chapters.title: Chapter 4530: Chase! I
paragraphs: The variations of Mana were unique in their versatility and applications.

With every Way he superseded and defeated, he could seamlessly mimic it as perfectly as the original. At this time, Noah stood atop Lumivara as his massive Early Creature body was maintained, but instead of the poisonous green brilliance he had been displaying, The Way of Existence he now expressed was that of crackling purple lightning arcing across his entire form!
He had killed and devoured six entities so far since being separated from Tor. Two had followed the Way of Poison, two the Way of Fire, one the Way of Mass, and one the Way of Lightning.
And his Primus Mana continued to become all that much more versatile as he could seamlessly mimic any of these Ways with complete authenticity.

Lumivara was genuinely astonished as she looked up at him from her position and asked with curious confusion, "Master, is your Way that of Mana, or Poison, or Lightning? You seem to shift between them so easily."
Noah replied with calm certainty, "Yes."
Lumivara blinked with incomprehension at such a simple answer.
"What does that mean, Master?" she asked with adorable confusion.
Noah replied calmly as he gazed ahead at his next target in the distance, a massive behemoth-like creature that resembled a wooly mammoth of titanic proportions.

"The spark you consumed showed you Mana and how your Light could be ever so glorious through proper understanding of its foundation," he explained with teaching patience. "My Mana can observe and mimic other Ways because I only follow Mana at its core,but I am also potentially following Everything since Mana has infinite variations and expressions."

His reply carried terrifying implications as he focused his perception on the 88 Decillion Mammoth in the distance. The creature pulsed with the Way of Defense, its entire existence dedicated to becoming impenetrable.
Noah observed analytically how this was a unique conceptual Way rather than an elemental one. Defense as an abstract principle rather than a physical manifestation.
So he chose to express Lightning for this encounter specifically for an extremely quick and penetrative result against this enemy.

And he could have chosen to manifest a bow or spear as the delivery mechanism for his long-range strike as he had done before. But he had more variations available to explore, and he could always try newer applications of his versatile Mana!

So he looked down at the visage of Lumivara beneath him and asked with measured curiosity, "What do you think for something designed for long-range devastation? A bow? A spear? A sniper rifle? Or perhaps a ballista? A nuclear warhead?"
Lumivara blinked with confusion at several of those terms.
"I am not familiar with some of those weapons, Master," she admitted honestly. "But the ballista seems interesting from how you said it?"
Noah smiled at her words. There were many applications of Mana he could experiment with in the future, weapons and tools from his memories of the blue planet and beyond.
But for now, he would indulge her curiosity.

A massive ballista began to form in the air above Lumivara, materializing from compressed lightning-infused Mana! The weapon was easily twice Noah’s current transformed size and pulsed dangerously with concentrated purple arcs of electricity that crackled with lethal intent.

Noah made a deliberate pulling motion with his hands, and a terrifying oversized arrow formed on the ballista. He poured immense waves of his Way of Mana and Hunger into the projectile, compressing it further and further.
He already had the True Expression of The Sovereignty of Mana and Hunger active from consuming an Unquantifiable Unit of Everything, so the arrow blazed withoverwhelmingauthority!
Below him, Lumivara’s eyes shone with awe and genuine marvel as she watched this terrifying weapon being prepared for release!
Noah looked at the distant mammoth with coldness as he spoke.

"Mana is the foundation of all interactions and changes in existence," he said with tyrannical certainty. "Defense is merely the resistance to change, the attempt to maintain a static state against external forces.But resistance requires energy, and that energy comes from Mana itself."
His eyes gleamed.

"So how can Defense powered by Mana ever truly stop an attack that asserts Mana’s dominion over that very defense? The defender. is using my foundation against me, which means I simply need to reclaim what is mine."
His logic was absolute in its confidence.
"And Hunger consumes all things, including the concept of protection itself. Defense cannot stand against the combination of these truths."
HUUM!
Then he released the ballista bolt!

The seemingly impenetrable massive Mammoth came to sudden attention as it sensed the incoming threat. Its body immediately shone with a brilliant bronze glow of concentrated defensive power, layers upon layers of protection manifesting instantly!
The creature had survived this long by making itself nearly invulnerable, and its instincts activated perfectly.
But it did not matter.
BOOM!
The ballista arrow struck with apocalyptic force! The purple lightning-infused projectile punched straight through the bronze defensive layers as if they were paper!
The Mammoth’s body was shot through and through, a massive hole carved from front to back! Crimson-gold blood spurted out in torrents as the creature’s Way of Defense collapsed entirely!
Noah looked at the scene with cold satisfaction as he already opened his jaw unnaturally wide. He beckoned toward the massive corpse, and it flew toward him through compressed space to be consumed!
Lumivara watched with cheerful excitement as her Master claimed another victory!
"The Master is very strong! The Master is the best!" she said with genuine enthusiasm. "Nothing could possibly take you down when you fight with such overwhelming-"
Before she could even finish such words of praise, both her and Noah’s expressions rapidly changed as they sensed something approaching!
HUUM!
Near them, a glimmer of white brilliance flared with sudden intensity! An entity radiating ecstatic power at the Pre-THE level appeared, materializing from concealment!
Her gaze was cold and callous as she looked at Noah and the fox he was mounted on with contempt and disdain!
In the picosecond where the Ambient Integration had been disrupted while Noah was decimating his enemy, a creature at Pre-THE had found their location!
Noah’s gaze became ice-cold as he recognized this entity immediately. She was one of the twelve Pre-THE existences thatTHE Time Surferhad brought with her, one of those actively hunting for him!
But she should in no way be able to recognize him in his current disguised state as...
The Pre-THE existence spoke with contemptuous disgust in her voice.

"I was wondering what that flickering Sovereignty of Light I sensed earlier was," she said while looking directly at Lumivara with hatred. "It seems to be a pathetic thing with no backbone that is acting as a mount for another? How utterly disgraceful."
Her eyes blazed with righteous fury.
"Let me put you out of your fucking misery. A creature like you does not deserve to walk The Way of Light!"
HUUM!
The moment she said such words with absolute conviction, this being of utterly terrible power that Noah was not ready for and could not currently decimate made her move!

She was at the level of Pre-THE Existences with her Sovereignty much more established than the creatures Noah had been hunting. She had made tremendous progress towardTHE Surface Depth of Absolute Sovereignty!
A status sheet flashed before Noah’s vision with alarming details.
|Name: Stellara, The Radiant Executioner|
|Classification: Light-Path Pre-THE Existence|
|Complexity: 997 Decillion|
|Purity: 997 Decillion|
|Grand Principles: Luminous Annihilation, Photonic Supremacy, Radiance Manifestation, Blinding Authority, Light Convergence, Brilliance Dominion, Purification Mastery, Illumination Genesis|
|Current Sovereignty Progress: 12.7% toward THE Surface Depth of Absolute Sovereignty|
|Status: Hostile - Intent to Kill|
Such a being erupted with imposing brilliance toward Noah and Lumivara!
And beneath Noah, Lumivara’s entire body trembled with primal terror as she recognized the power difference!

chapters.title: Chapter 4531: Chase! II
paragraphs: Light.

At its most fundamental level, light was electromagnetic radiation traveling through space as both wave and particle. Photons carrying energy across the void, moving at speeds that conventional understanding deemed absolute.
But that was merely surface understanding.

Light was also information made visible. The ability to observe and perceive one’s surroundings through electromagnetic interaction. It revealed truths while creating shadows that concealed them. It could be gentle warmth or searing devastation depending on concentration.
And at the deepest level, light was simply energy...Mana manifesting as electromagnetic force.
Which meant it could be understood and superseded.

When it came to Light as a Way of Existence, Noah had already superseded this path through his connection with Lumivara. Through the spark of Mana she had consumed, through observing how Light connected to his fundamental Way, he had gained understanding that allowed him to exert influence over this Sovereignty.

This was why even though a terrifying Pre-THE Existence had appeared with murderous intent, he did not consider the situation catastrophic. His Way of Mana and Hunger could exert tremendous effect against Light, even if the enemy was extremely advanced in her Sovereignty.
So the moment Stellara erupted with her Way, Noah responded.

Tendrils of purple lightning exploded from his body, but he was not forming anything long-ranged or close-ranged. Instead, he manifested extremely compressed concentrations of The True Expression of The Sovereignty of Mana and Hunger contained inside a weapon of mass destruction.
The concept of a nuclear warhead, reimagined through his Way.

A radiant purple statue materialized between them and Stellara. The statue resembled a rotund version of Noah’s current form with an enormous belly pulsing with compressed authority. Its expression mixed devilish malevolence with benevolent serenity, like some corrupted entity containing obliteration within stillness.
The statue’s eyes opened as white light washed over it.
And then it detonated.
This time, Noah was not containing the damage. He would unleash devastation without restraint!
BOOOOOOM!

The explosion was apocalyptic in scale. A sphere of purple lightning-infused Mana expanded outward with violent force, fracturing reality around the epicenter. The shockwave propagated for light-years in every direction, distorting space and shattering matter.
The two sides were pushed violently apart. Mountains crumbled, ancient trees disintegrated, and the ground collapsed into nothingness.
Noah patted Lumivara’s fur with measured urgency as he spoke. "Run far and run fast. Do not look back."
Lumivara’s body transformed into pure light as she activated her Way to its fullest extent. Her form became almost intangible, moving at speeds approaching theoretical maximum of the very idea speed!
She was light! She was speed!
WAA!
Behind them, Stellara emerged from the dissipating explosion with shock transforming into fury.
"You would flee from judgment?" she called out, her voice carrying weight that pressed against existence.
She began a pursuit with terrifying determination!
Her body became wreathed in white brilliance so intense it seemed to burn away the space around her. She launched forward with speed that would have overtaken any normal Light-path entity instantly.
But Lumivara was no longer normal.
"Master!" Lumivara said with controlled tension. "Her Sovereignty is too developed! I cannot..."
Noah remained calm, his hands glowing with concentrated Mana that he channeled directly into Lumivara’s existence.
"Your Light is no longer solely yours," he said with measured certainty. "It is amplified by Mana’s infinite reservoir. Draw on what I provide without reservation."

Lumivara felt the surge of power- a surge of an utterly glorious Way of Existence flooding through her and her speed increased dramatically. Her Way of Light became supercharged by Noah’s contribution, surpassing her absolute limits.
Behind them, Stellara roared with frustration as the distance refused to close!
She was a Pre-THE Existence chasing weaker entities that barely had ties to their Sovereignties! What the fuck was this?!

They crossed through a region of floating crystalline formations that refracted light in dizzying patterns. Lumivara wove through them with instinctive grace while Stellara smashed through them with brute force, creating explosions of shattered crystal.
"You are merely delaying the inevitable," Stellara roared with cold certainty. "I have dedicated my existence to purifying the Way of Light from those unworthy to walk it!"
HUUM!
Noah glanced back with calculating eyes and spoke calmly to Lumivara.
"Continue as is," he said. "Take us toward that wormhole you mentioned. The passage leading to your Sanctuary of Perpetual Dawn."
Lumivara’s eyes widened with shock.
"Master, that domain holds immense unknown dangers..." she said while continuing to run. "Are you...sure?"
Noah’s voice carried absolute command. "She will pursue regardless of direction. At least in that domain, there may be variables we can exploit. Go."
Lumivara hesitated briefly before complying. If The Master commanded it,she would obey.
Mana and Light burned together gloriously as their figures radiated a profound purple white luster- especially the royal tyrannical purple as Noah kept the way of Lightning circling around him!
They crossed vast regions in compressed moments, traveling distances that would require even the Dukes of Living Existences in the current era days to traverse!
Through primordial forests, over mountains scraping the atmosphere, across valleys filled with mist concealing ancient dangers!
Across the murky and misty regions of The Infinite Unfurling, Stellara pursued relentlessly, her white brilliance a constant presence!

"You disgrace everything Light represents with your cowardice!" she said with righteous conviction. "If you possessed even a fragment of worthiness, you would stand and face judgment rather than scurrying like vermin!"

Noah remained calm as every now and then, he would stand atop Lumivara and throw back a radiant purple spear or a warhead, eventually forming an illusory bow to manifest behind him as it released bursts of purple mixed with white of His Way and The Way of Light!
All of it...infuriated and slowed down Stellara to no end.
Until minutes later, after having to utilize multiple Unquantifiable Units of Everything...
They approached a region where space shimmered with subtle distortion. Lumivara’s eyes locked onto a specific point that appeared empty to standard perception.
"There, Master. The wormhole entrance," she said with desperate hope.
Noah’s perception focused on the location and he could barely detect the spatial anomaly. It was extraordinarily well-concealed, almost invisible even to his enhanced senses.
Lumivara did not decelerate as they approached. Instead, she accelerated harder.
"Master, maintain your grip," she warned.
And then they plunged into the wormhole.
HUUM!
Reality twisted around them in configurations defying understanding. Space compressed and expanded simultaneously. They were moving forward and backward and sideways all at once!
The sensation lasted both an eternity and a single instant before they emerged in a completely different region.
Lumivara’s eyes blazed with focus as she searched for the specific frequency of light that would reveal the true entrance.
"Master, I need to isolate the exact wavelength," she said with strained concentration. "It shifts across temporal and light intervals and I need to... there!"
Her perception locked onto a unique oscillation invisible to standard observation. A doorway that existed only for those who understood precisely where to look.
A point of brilliant light.
She adjusted trajectory and passed through the frequency barrier.
POP!
The world transformed with jarring immediacy.
And Noah felt...an eruption of brilliance that caused his existence to pulse with euphoria!
They found themselves in a domain where light existed in its purest form. Brilliance blazed from every direction with intensity that would blind lesser beings permanently.
Even Noah’s eyes were acclimatint to be able to clearly see in this region of blinding light!
A sense pressure was immediate and oppressive, pushing down on their existences with crushing force.

"Master, we have entered the Sanctuary of Perpetual Dawn," Lumivara said with voice strained by effort. "I can only sustain my position in the outer periphery. Venturing deeper would be catastrophic for me. And that savage woman may or may not discover thst unique frequency of light as it took me some time, so we may only have a few minutes here!"
Lumivara spoke with urgency.
Noah looked around with analytical fascination despite the dangerous circumstances. The domain...was unlike anything he had encountered!

chapters.title: Chapter 4532: The Distraught and The Defiant! I
paragraphs: As soon as Noah entered the domain, his entire existence began buzzing with recognition and absorption as the environment proved to beextraordinarilynutrient rich.

Nutrient rich was not even adequate to describe what he was experiencing. It felt like a singular natal component of existence was present here in its most pure and concentrated form, and his body was continuously drinking it in without conscious effort.
Even more interesting was the fact that every single particle of this atmospheric authority that flowed into him was traveling directly intoTHE Organ of Civilization.
Directly into his head where that unfathomable wonder that had not existed in Observable Existence before his design of it continued to rotate with increasing intensity.

As it drank in this glorious authority with ravenous efficiency, Noah’s eyes seemingly adjusted to the blinding radiance little by little. The first thing that he could perceive clearly was the emergence of prompts blooming before his vision.
|You have arrived in THE Northern Unfurling Node of Existence of THE Creature|
|Classification: Ancient Sealed Domain|
|Primary Function:Concentration and preservation of THE Civilizational Authority|
|Environmental Characteristics: Authority at the level ofTHEbecomes trapped within this domain and concentrates in increasingly high density the further inward one travels.|
|Natural Phenomenon: These dense concentrations of pureTHE Civilizational Authoritycan crystallize and form into natural treasures of immense value.|

|Pressure Mechanics: The atmospheric authority naturally generates pressure befitting its concentrated nature. Entities belowTHEscale will experience increasing difficulty sustaining existence the deeper they venture.|
|Warning: This domain operates under principles designed byTHE Creaturefor purposes unknown.|
|Current Location: Outer Periphery (Lowest concentration zone)|
Noah’s eyes opened wide with surprise at such a terrifying array of knowledge being revealed.
THE Northern Unfurling Node of Existence of THE Creature.
Northern meant there were at least three other places exactly like this one scattered across the Infinite Unfurling. Possibly more.

And what was terrifying enough was these domains having Unfurling in their name alongside the direct distinction of belonging toTHE Creature. As if this entire construct had been designed and built byTHE Creaturefor specific purposes.
What the hell was this place actually meant to accomplish?

Noah’s eyes remained stern and analytical as the surroundings became slightly more clear while his existence continued to passively absorb what should be an extremely pure and concentrated form ofTHE Civilizational Authority.
The region he could now observe was actually quite beautiful in its simplicity.

A halo of brilliant white light covered everything like a gentle blanket, creating an atmosphere of perpetual dawn. Before him stretched a serene landscape of lush grasslands dotted with flowers that swayed despite there being no wind. Floating landmasses hovered above the ground, each one pulsing with ecstatic authority that resonated through space.

The entire place actually looked surprisingly empty and not overly complex in its construction. Apart from this area of grassland and the few floating landmasses, there were only scattered trees rising here and there. But each tree radiated terrifying levels of concentrated authority that made them seem almost alive with purpose.
That was everything he could currently perceive in this outer region.
But this was clearly only the periphery of something much larger.

When his eyes tracked further inward toward the center, he saw another distinct ring of white light that seemed to mark the boundary into a much more concentrated domain. His vision did not extend beyond that luminous barrier, as if his perception was being actively blocked.

He would have to physically pass the line that distinguished the outer periphery from the inner regions for him to be capable of seeing and perceiving what truly lay inside of this terrifying place known asTHE Northern Unfurling Node of Existence of THE Creature.
But as he was observing and thinking analytically about all of this information...
BOOM!
His existence buzzed with sudden intensity as he feltTHE Organ of Civilizationin his head reach a significant milestone while it was crazily absorbing the atmospheric authority around them.
New prompts flashed before his vision.
|THE Organ of Civilization Progress: 1% toward THE Surface Depth of Absolute Sovereignty|
|Unquantifiable Units of Everything: 11/20 (Regeneration continuing)|
|THE Organ of Civilizationhas reached an important developmental threshold.|
|Progress Status: One hundredth of the way toward complete establishment ofTHE Surface Depth.|
|Advancement Unlocked: The Unquantifiable Units of Everything produced by THE Organ of Civilization have been refined and quantified.|
|New Classification: THE Rudimentary Units of Everything|
|Effect: Units now possess defined properties and applications rather than purely conceptual existence.|
THE Rudimentary Units of Everything.
Oh!

Noah looked at this unique distinction with analytical interest as he examined the mobius strips of wonder that floated within his existence. The transformation from unquantifiable to rudimentary was progress toward something more refined.
Another prompt materialized with defining information.
|THE RUDIMENTARY UNITS OF EVERYTHING|
|Classification: Nascent form of ultimate authority currency|
|Nature: Concentrated essence of civilizational potential that can be applied to any concept, principle, or expression of existence.|
|Current Capabilities: Can fuel THE True Expression of Sovereignty. Can accelerate growth of THE Organ of Civilization. Can be consumed to temporarily enhance any aspect of existence.|
|Limitations: Rudimentary nature means efficiency is lower than more refined versions. Maximum storage capacity currently limited to 20 units.|
|Progression Path: Will evolve into more potent forms asTHE Organ of Civilizationdeepens.|
|Note: These units represent the foundation of something.|
Noah looked at the detailed information with eyes shining with Quintessence. His progress was accelerating faster than he had anticipated!
Nearby, the figure of Lumivara underwent a startling transformation as her body shifted from into a humanoid shape.

She appeared as a young woman with delicate features and pale skin that seemed to glow with inner light. Her hair was long and white with an almost liquid quality, flowing down her back like starlight given form.
Fox ears protruded from the top of her head, twitching with nervous energy. A single lush fox tail emerged from the base of her spine, swaying gently.
She wore simple white robes that seemed to be woven from light itself, and her golden eyes looked around with an expression of complete awe.

"Master, what is happening to me?" she asked with wonder coloring her voice. "When I came here before, I could only gain power and advance my Sovereignty by venturing slightly further inward and plucking fruits from those trees over there."
She gestured toward the scattered trees pulsing with authority.
"But now it seems my body is innately attracting the atmospheric authority without any effort on my part. Is this because of... Master’s Mana connected to my existence?"

chapters.title: Chapter 4533: The Distraught and The Defiant! II
paragraphs: Lumivara had revealed a shocking piece of information through her observation.

The reason Noah was able to freely absorb the surrounding atmosphere was potentially due to his own grand Way and how it related to everything as foundational authority. And through their connection, Lumivara was benefiting from the same principle.
There was clearly much to learn about this place and exactly how much of an opportunity all of this represented. But before he could truly delve into investigation and exploration...
BOOM!
Space behind them squeezed and compressed violently before spitting something else through the frequency barrier.

The visage of none other than Stellara appeared with an expression of absolute fury written across her luminous features. Her eyes locked onto Noah and Lumivara with murderous intent that needed no verbal expression!
Lumivara immediately moved to hide behind Noah’s transformed body, her earlier confidence evaporating in the face of this overwhelming threat.
But at this moment, Noah did not run from the Pre-THE Existence. Nor did he erupt with any defensive authority or prepare offensive measures.
He simply looked at the figure before him with calm analytical assessment as a thought occurred to him.
Pre-THE was still partly at the level of THE, correct? The designation itself suggested they had one foot in that realm even if not fully established.
Which meant...
A moment after he had such a thought, the figure of Stellara opened her mouth to begin bellowing threats and condemnation.
But in the next instant, something shocking occurred.
HUUM!

Space above her seemingly squeezed and compressed with invisible force. In a shocking flow of events that Stellara had anticipated, the glorious and deadly authority that composed this Pre-THE being’s power began to be forcefully drawn out of her body!
Her Sovereignty was being absorbed directly into the surrounding atmosphere.
Stellara’s eyes widened with horror as she felt her carefully cultivated authority being stripped away without her consent or ability to resist.
And Noah watched with cold eyes as the domain did exactly what the prompts had warned it would do!
It trapped and concentrated authority at the level ofTHE.
And apparently, it did not distinguish between fully establishedTHEentities and those who were deemed asPre-THE!
Oh!
Losing one’s power... was never something to take lightly.
It was akin to a billionaire watching their portfolio and seeing hundreds of millions rapidly evaporating every second without being able to do anything to stop the hemorrhaging losses.

It was akin to a king who ruled multiple continents watching his dominion being carved apart and taken by foreign conquerors, as his harem of women was divided among different victors as spoils of war.
It was absolutely not a pleasant experience under any circumstances.
And Stellara felt this reality with crushing intimacy at this precise moment as Noah observed her shockingly losing her designation as a Pre-THE Existence.

His perceptive eyes analyzed the situation rapidly as on her status sheet, he actually witnessed her Current Sovereignty Progress that had been at12.7% toward THE Surface Depth of Absolute Sovereigntybegin to rapidly decrease. It only slowed its decline after dropping below the 10% threshold.
And then, on her status sheet, her designation actually lost the Pre-THE Existence classification entirely!
Ten percent.

Was this the marker that one had to surpass towardTHE Surface Depth of Absolute Sovereigntybefore they could be considered a Pre-THE Existence? A hard boundary that separated the truly progressed from those merely attempting the path?

And did this also equate to the same percentage threshold that he had observed for the completion ofTHE Organ of Civilization?If he reached 10% completion with it, he would be considered a Pre-THE Existence?
He filed these observations away in the back of his mind for further contemplation later. For now, he looked at the figure of Stellara who appeared as if she had lost her very heart and soul.
And truly, she had lost something equivalently devastating.
Her Way that she had worked so extraordinarily hard to cultivate had effectively been reduced to a fraction of its former power by this domain’s mechanisms.
And now, even though she was still unfathomably more powerful than Noah in raw statistics...
Noah began walking toward her with measured steps as his eyes flashed with an extremely tyrannical and quintessential light.
"Hey, it looks like you have run into some ratherunfortunatecircumstances," he said with dark satisfaction coloring his words. "Allow me to lend you a helping hand in your time of need."

As he spoke with false sympathy, he burned another Rudimentary Unit of Everything. His existence began to radiate profound and glorious luster as THE True Expression of The Sovereignty of Mana and Hunger activated once more, and after the revent advancement ofTHE Organ of Civilization, this state felt stronger than ever!
He...was truly getting stronger!

He threw his hand back in a familiar motion and formed a tyrannical purple spear of concentrated lightning. Without hesitation, he hurled it toward the distraught Stellara who had just lost a catastrophic chunk of her carefully cultivated power.

Take care of this enemy first, and then he could fully enjoy and explore this terrifying place that he had stumbled into by fortunate accident. This place that bore the name ofTHE Creaturein its very designation!
The past was the past and the present was the present.
The changes made in the past would not manifest their effects in the future until the one making these alterations actually returned to their original timeline.

Because as of this moment, nothing was truly set in stone. If an entity traveled into the past and perished there, one could legitimately wonder how the paradox of temporal causality would be resolved. When it came to time and its manipulation, there were far too many intricacies and variables to account for.
But at this moment, an unfathomably far distance of time past the Infinite Unfurling, in the current era that Noah had originated from...
In a domain that could not be found in The Folds or The Wandering Territories. In a space between spaces where normal rules of reality did not fully apply.
In that unique domain where the figures of Sigrid and Noah used to sit beside one another on opposite sides of the veil, there now remained onlyTHE Dead Order and Sigrid!

chapters.title: Chapter 4534: The Distraught and The Defiant! III
paragraphs: At this moment, Sigrid was actually alone on her side of the translucent barrier. On the other side of the veil, the radiant wall of Order that had been veiling and shieldingTHE Dead Orderfrom direct observation actually began to fade away with deliberate purpose.
This glorious entity seated upon her throne of compressed authority looked directly at Sigrid with a calculating assessment.
She observed the situation closely, noting how Sigrid sat alone at this moment. Her eyes shone with sharp ingenuity as she spoke with measured curiosity.

"He disappeared rather abruptly, did he not?" THE Dead Ordersaid with false concern. "I sincerely doubt he would ever voluntarily leave you here alone with me given his protective nature. So tell me, could he simply not handle the curse of THE Living Elemental any longer? Did something catastrophic happen to him that forced his departure?"
She asked such a pivotal question with the tone of someone already knowing the answer.
Sigrid’s expression remained composed as she replied with cold certainty.

"You witnessed him handling those flames perfectly well before," she said without emotion. "Is it because you are personally so weak yourself that after feeling them briefly upon your own existence, you would automatically assume that he would not be able to survive their effects? No, he is not nearly as weak-willed as you have proven yourself to be."
THE Dead Orderlaughed with genuine amusement at the response.

"Haha, nice attempt at deflection, you dirtied whore of a vessel," she said with condescension dripping from every word. "No, he would not leave you here alone with me under normal circumstances. He clearly favors you far too much for such carelessness."
Her expression became more serious as she continued.

"You see, those are precisely the types of entanglements that inevitably arise when one desecrates the principles of Order. You form these attachments, these emotional entanglements that do nothing but lead directly to Chaos and instability. To the point where one’s existence would physically ache for another’s presence."
She rose slowly from her throne.

"It is so widespread across all of existence that one of the most powerful Living Existences has built their entire power structure based purely on emotions and their manipulation. All because of pathetic little creatures like you who do not possess adequate control over your feelings and impulses."
Her words were biting and cold as ice as she began walking toward the veil separating them.

"And precisely because of those feelings, because of those debilitating emotions that cloud judgment, I will graciously offer you a way out of your predicament," she said with false benevolence. "I possess the capability to help him properly manage those cursed flames as he wanted before they inevitably consume him and cause complete collapse."
She gestured to herself.

"Look at me now, child. The flames that he so foolishly spread onto my existence when we touched... I have successfully taken care of them completely. It required slightly more of my accumulated power than I would have preferred to expend, but it was manageable nonetheless."
Her eyes gleamed with predatory intent.
"I can perform the exact same service for your dear Osmont. So let us strike a mutually beneficial deal here and now. Trade... yourself to save him from certain death."
BOOM!
Sigrid’s eyes flashed sharply at these manipulative words asTHE Dead Ordercontinued her proposition.

"Simply come over and cross to this side of the veil and give yourself willingly to me," she said while extending her hand in invitation. "And I will make a binding promise on my very existence and on Order itself that I will not bring harm to your Osmont or to the nascent flicker of his Civilization."
Her voice became almost tender.

"Come and fuse with me completely. Become one with the grander and infinitely greater power of pure Order, and let me help both you and your Osmont survive THE Loom’s machinations. Come, child. Let us put all of this past conflict behind us and move forward together. Come to Ama."
THE Dead Orderspoke such words while extending her hand outward in an inviting fashion that appeared almost maternal in its gesture.

Sigrid floated closer and closer toward the veil with a complex expression playing across her features. Her movements were slow and deliberate as if she was genuinely considering the offer being presented.
She stopped directly in front of the translucent barrier and reached out with her hand. Her fingers came to rest gently upon the surface of the veil.
THE Dead Orderlooked at her with grand anticipation building in her ancient eyes.

"Just a few more steps, child," she encouraged with barely concealed eagerness. "Cross over and unfathomable glory will be yours. You will have survived The Fallout that would destroy so much. You will have transcended your current limitations."
HUUM!
At such a critical moment, Sigrid’s expression shifted into a genuine smile.
"I wanted to come by real close to you," she said with calm satisfaction, "to tell you something important."
She paused for effect.
"No."
BOOM!
Her singular word of absolute rejection caused the expression ofTHE Dead Orderto transform from anticipation to something exceedingly cold and utterly apathetic.
Sigrid continued speaking.

"He does not appreciate sacrifices made on his behalf," she said with conviction resonating through every syllable. "He keeps expressing this preference time and time again, to the point where you would think existence itself would finally understand the message he is sending."
Her eyes blazed with defiant determination.
"But apparently not. So let me make this abundantly clear: No sacrifices will be made. And if you have truly taken care of the curse ofTHE Living Elementalas you claim..."
HUUM!

Sigrid clenched her fist with decisive action. In the next moment, a massive river of Order began flowing fromTHE Dead Order’sside directly toward her position. The siphoning process that she had voluntarily stopped earlier was now returned with even grander intensity than before.
THE Dead Orderlooked at this development with extremely cold and apathetic eyes. She did not immediately issue any threats or even speak at all for several long seconds.
As if she was simply taking in the full measure of Sigrid’s figure and committing this moment of defiance to eternal memory.
The silence stretched uncomfortably before she finally spoke with a measured tone.

"You have lost your protector," she said with clinical observation. "While he is currently incapable of intervening or may have even collapsed entirely from the curse of THE Living Elemental, I will now make my move against you."
WAA!
Her eyes narrowed with predatory focus.

"I believe I will begin by activating one of the Disciples of THE Creature that remain dormant across existence. They might manifest at False THE level of power, or perhaps even higher depending on variables. We shall observe what emerges."
She tilted her head with false curiosity.
"What say you, child? Will you stubbornly continue to stay on this self-destructive path you have chosen?"
Would she stay on this path of defiance and resistance?

Sigrid’s eyes shone with a sense of tyranny that she had only ever witnessed within Noah’s gaze when he was at his most determined. When he was absolutely certain of victory regardless of circumstances.
"Bring it the fuck on, you decrepit old hag,"she said with absolute conviction and zero hesitation.

So let us strike a mutually beneficial deal here and now.
Trade... yourself to save him from certain death."
BOOM!
Sigrid’s eyes flashed sharply at these manipulative words asTHE Dead Ordercontinued her proposition.
"Simply come over and cross to this side of the veil and give yourself willingly to me," she said while extending her hand in invitation.
"And I will make a binding promise on my very existence and on Order itself that I will not bring harm to your Osmont or to the nascent flicker of his Civilization."
Her voice became almost tender.
"Come and fuse with me completely.
Become one with the grander and infinitely greater power of pure Order, and let me help both you and your Osmont survive THE Loom’s machinations.
Come, child.
Let us put all of this past conflict behind us and move forward together.
Come to Ama."
THE Dead Orderspoke such words while extending her hand outward in an inviting fashion that appeared almost maternal in its gesture.
Sigrid floated closer and closer toward the veil with a complex expression playing across her features.
Her movements were slow and deliberate as if she was genuinely considering the offer being presented.
She stopped directly in front of the translucent barrier and reached out with her hand.
Her fingers came to rest gently upon the surface of the veil.
THE Dead Orderlooked at her with grand anticipation building in her ancient eyes.
"Just a few more steps, child," she encouraged with barely concealed eagerness.
"Cross over and unfathomable glory will be yours.
You will have survived The Fallout that would destroy so much.
You will have transcended your current limitations."
HUUM!
At such a critical moment, Sigrid’s expression shifted into a genuine smile.
"I wanted to come by real close to you," she said with calm satisfaction, "to tell you something important."
She paused for effect.
"No."
BOOM!
Her singular word of absolute rejection caused the expression ofTHE Dead Orderto transform from anticipation to something exceedingly cold and utterly apathetic.
Sigrid continued speaking.
"He does not appreciate sacrifices made on his behalf," she said with conviction resonating through every syllable.
"He keeps expressing this preference time and time again, to the point where you would think existence itself would finally understand the message he is sending."
Her eyes blazed with defiant determination.
"But apparently not.
So let me make this abundantly clear: No sacrifices will be made.
And if you have truly taken care of the curse ofTHE Living Elementalas you claim..."
HUUM!
Sigrid clenched her fist with decisive action.
In the next moment, a massive river of Order began flowing fromTHE Dead Order’sside directly toward her position.
The siphoning process that she had voluntarily stopped earlier was now returned with even grander intensity than before.
THE Dead Orderlooked at this development with extremely cold and apathetic eyes.
She did not immediately issue any threats or even speak at all for several long seconds.
As if she was simply taking in the full measure of Sigrid’s figure and committing this moment of defiance to eternal memory.
The silence stretched uncomfortably before she finally spoke with a measured tone.
"You have lost your protector," she said with clinical observation.
"While he is currently incapable of intervening or may have even collapsed entirely from the curse of THE Living Elemental, I will now make my move against you."
WAA!
Her eyes narrowed with predatory focus.
"I believe I will begin by activating one of the Disciples of THE Creature that remain dormant across existence.
They might manifest at False THE level of power, or perhaps even higher depending on variables.
We shall observe what emerges."
She tilted her head with false curiosity.
"What say you, child?
Will you stubbornly continue to stay on this self-destructive path you have chosen?"
Would she stay on this path of defiance and resistance?
Sigrid’s eyes shone with a sense of tyranny that she had only ever witnessed within Noah’s gaze when he was at his most determined.
When he was absolutely certain of victory regardless of circumstances.
"Bring it the fuck on, you decrepit old hag,"she said with absolute conviction and zero hesitation.

chapters.title: Chapter 4535: The Distraught and The Defiant! IV
paragraphs: In the Early Veiled Shore.

Sigrid felt the golden sands beneath her feet as she looked out at this now massive continent that seemed to be expanding with every passing second. The growth was subtle but constant, like watching a child mature in accelerated time.

The plots filled with sacred herbs continued to increase in number as they were tended to without issue by automated systems and literal Tenders. Marine lifeforms continued to be caught and cataloged in the massive Aquarium as it filled with scintillating multicolored creatures from across different realities.

Massive Sovereign Spires of Osmont could be seen in various corners of this continent, each one pulsing with authority. Armies of Primus Inevitabilities were constantly flowing into these structures to undergo Civilization Specialization, emerging stronger and more capable than when they entered.

The entire domain felt like a grand unfolding of life and existence. Like something sacred that someone had cultivated from a very small point and raised and elevated up to its current impressive stage through dedication and vision.

She had not been present when Noah first began building the Early Veiled Shore, but he had described it to her with fondness. How its size was tiny initially with just a few trees scattered here and there and barely any cultivation plots. How he had fought against a goldfish!
She smiled at the memory. Even if he was not physically here at this moment, she wanted to be able to protect such a place. She wanted to be able to safeguard his home and everything he had built.
So she closed her eyes and sent out her voice and intent to multiple people across the domain through their connections.
And moments later, space rippled as figures began materializing.

Multiple beings began to surround the golden sands where Sigrid stood. They included The Infiniverse with her flowing form of Omniverses and verdant-gold light. Khor with her obsidian-crimson aura of Hunger. Protos in his crystalline magnificence. Riya with her blazing blue eyes and Kael radiating discipline.
There was Henry carrying Noah’s bloodline authority. Moiraine and Malphas exuding dark power. Adelaide shining with immensity, and Barbatos wrapped in deathly shadows!
They all appeared around her in a semicircle as Sigrid looked at each of them in turn before speaking.

"THE Dead Orderplans to send forth a Disciple ofTHE Creatureinto the lands of the living," she said with measured calm. "Directed specifically toward us. Such an entity could potentially be at the level of False THE in power. She may also likely send along her Guiders of Order as additional forces."
She paused before adding the most important detail.
"And he is not here to protect us."
He.

They all knew immediately who she was referencing at this moment. For the first time since their collective rise to power, a significant threat was approaching while they did not have Noah’s direct protection or intervention available.
The figure of Henry looked at everyone gathered before speaking with calm confidence.
"Even when Father is not physically present, his power and foundation still remain with us," he said with conviction and Nepotism resonating through his words!
"Whatever forces they throw at us should not prove insurmountable. We are not helpless children."
His words were filled with genuine calm and unshakeable confidence. After he spoke, Sigrid nodded with acknowledgment before looking toward the others assembled.
At this moment, all heads gradually turned to focus on none other than The Infiniverse and Khor. The two most powerful entities present aside from Sigrid herself.
The gazes of these two women shone with imperious and regal allure as they processed the information.
Khor spoke first with a sense of aged wisdom!

"THE Dead Orderis a vindictive bitch who carries considerable baggage and unresolved trauma," she said with cold observation. "She remains the only THE Living Existence to have been collapsed and defeated in that catastrophic battle all those years ago. Her pride has never recovered..."
Her eyes gleamed with dark understanding.

"She will absolutely do what she threatens because proving her continued relevance is necessary for her. The only variable we control is our adequate response to her aggression. Since we cannot venture into the lands of the dead to strike first, we can only wait here and prepare ourselves to be ready for whatever emerges."
She crossed her arms with thoughtful consideration.
"With the capabilities of Civilization Specialization and the millions of Primus Inevitabilities at our disposal, it may not be merely a pipe dream to successfully stand against a False THE entity."
Khor quieted after these measured words, and many eyes shifted expectantly toward The Infiniverse next.
Her gaze was calm and supremely commanding as she spoke.
"The Master has already positioned someone in the lands of the dead who is not perceivable even to the awareness ofTHE Dead Orderherself," she revealed with confidence.
"I will establish communication with this being to gather intelligence on exactly what forces will emerge from the lands of the dead and when we can expect their arrival."
Her form pulsed with authority.

"We are currently positioned within the Wandering Territories. Locating our exact position will require considerable time and resources, if they succeed in finding us at all. And in the case that they do manage to track us down..."
Her voice became predatory.

"They will simply become another target of conquest for me to systematically devour and integrate. Let her send whatever forces she desires. The Primus Inevitabilities will be prepared and positioned. The specialized legions will be ready. I will coordinate everything personally to ensure maximum efficiency."
BOOM!
Her words radiated terrifying commanding allure that left no room for doubt or fear. After she finished speaking, her brilliant figure disappeared immediately without further discussion.
She genuinely did not fear whatever threats were coming toward them.

Sigrid smiled as she looked down at the footprints in the golden sand where The Infiniverse had just been standing moments before. She was not alone in this defense, and nobody was demanding that she sacrifice herself to protect them. She had found genuinely good people to surround herself with.
The future held untold possibilities and challenges, but they would face them as they came.
And as forTHE Dead Orderwho actually believed that they had lost their protector and become vulnerable?
She would come to learn otherwise soon enough!

chapters.title: Chapter 4536: The Illusion of Choice I
paragraphs: Across the Transcendent Folds, the Wandering Territories, and regions of endless collapse, there existed domains that defied categorization.
In another such domain that could be considered a space between spaces, where reality operated under different principles entirely, a figure stirred in an iridescent gold-obsidian paradoxical sea.
Schrodinger woke slowly, as if emerging from a long dream that had lasted far longer than it should have.

He wore his familiar tattered beggar’s robes that hung loosely on his frame, threadbare and worn from countless journeys. The fabric was patched in multiple places with materials that did not quite match, giving him the appearance of someone who had wandered through existence collecting scraps along the way.
As he blinked and consciousness fully returned, he heard a voice that caused his awareness to sharpen immediately.

The voice was filled with an air of glory and command of immense power, and yet it was also suffused with a palpable sense of mischievousness. Like someone playing a game they had already won but were enjoying the process of revealing that victory.
"Hey there, big guy," the voice said with casual familiarity. "You were asleep for quite some time."
The words caused Schrodinger to frown as he looked around the paradoxical sea surrounding him. In front of his figure, the obsidian-gold liquid began converging together with purposeful movement.

It formed another humanoid shape that looked exactly like him in basic structure, but the expression on this duplicate’s face was filled with a sense of majesty mixed with a playful smile that Schrodinger had never worn himself.
Schrodinger’s expression became extremely heavy as he looked at this being. His entire existence was seemingly screaming out the identity of the person manifesting before him.
"Are you..." he said with voice tight with tension. "Am I truly just a part ofTHE Living Paradox?"
The body ofTHE Living Paradoxsmiled with genuine amusement at the question.

"You were always merely a shred of my weavings," he said with casual acknowledgment. "But you developed autonomy over time and fully separated from my direct control. It happens occasionally with fragments that are given enough space to grow."
He tilted his head with a philosophical consideration.

"You know, all the countless lifeforms across existence genuinely believe they possess some form or sense of autonomy or choice. That they make decisions independent of external factors and that their will is truly their own."
He gestured broadly at nothing in particular.

"But really? Every illusion of autonomy or choice is fundamentally informed by their surroundings and circumstances. If you want to pursue a certain profession, you must exist in an environment that even has that profession available. If you want to become strong but you are born without talent or capability, you will never achieve that strength no matter how much you desire it."
His smile became almost pitying.

"If you wish to see but you are born blind, what the hell can you actually do about that limitation? Autonomy is vastly overrated, even if your existence genuinely believes that you developed it and have been your own separate being operating independently this whole time."
Schrodinger listened to such words with an extremely cloudy expression before he shook his head with visible rejection.
"No," he said with quiet conviction. "I lived as me. I loved as me. I made decisions and took actions out of my own volition. I never even knew of your weavings of existence until this very moment."
At such words,THE Living Paradoxlaughed with genuine entertainment.
"Sure, buddy," he said with condescending amusement. "You go on believing that comfortable narrative if it helps you process this."
An immense silence settled between them before Schrodinger asked another question that had been weighing on him.
"THE Weaversappeared before me," he began, but before his words could even finish forming completely,THE Living Paradoxwaved his hands dismissively.

"Don’t even worry about that little incident,"he said with casual unconcern. "They were just checking up on things and steering my vessel in the right direction. Standard procedure for entities of their function. But hey, why don’t you ask the proper question right now instead of dancing around what you really want to know?"
The proper question.
Once Schrodinger heard such pointed words, his eyes flashed with a sense of power as he spoke with direct clarity.
"Why am I here?" he asked without elaboration.
THE Living Paradoxsmiled with satisfaction.

"A lot of people actually think a lot of different things regarding who I am or what I fundamentally stand for," he said with measured consideration."To say I simply stand for paradox itself is a severe understatement. To say that I stand for anything else besides that is disrespecting the very nature of paradox."
He shrugged with casual indifference.

"But for the most part, I really am just a simple existence when you strip away all the mystique. I am driven by the same basic things that drive all other countless lifeforms out there. I am not some big scary bad guy, nor am I some benevolent saint. I am just me, pursuing what interests me."
As he spoke these words, the paradoxical sea around them churned with increased intensity. The obsidian and gold swirled in patterns that hurt to observe directly.

"Many people have consistently misunderstood me over the ages," he continued with something resembling mild frustration. "Some think I am their greatest enemy when I genuinely could not give a damn about them or their struggles. Others think I am their strongest ally when I am simply using them because circumstances made that convenient."
His expression became more serious.

"Some will think they have formed such a strong and irrevocable attachment to me that I could never possibly do them wrong or betray their trust. Many of them fundamentally misunderstand the nature of our relationship. The only entity that I truly care anything substantial about is THE Creature."
BOOM!
His words carried weight that pressed against existence itself as Schrodinger continued to listen with an even heavier expression settling across his features.
THE Living Paradoxcontinued speaking with unusual candor.

"You know, me and THE Creature are engaged in a race,"he said with intensity entering his casual tone."A race of existential innovation where the one who makes the critical breakthrough and attains The Second Civilizational Scale of Existence is the one who wins. The only one who wins everything."
He emphasized those last words.

"It is a race against time itself. A race of pure innovation and capability. I have to prove myself and demonstrate my superiority over existence without any question or doubt remaining. And my only real enemy in this endeavor is THE Creature, which is fucking scarier than you can even begin to imagine."
His eyes gleamed with something that might have been respect or fear.

"So I have to do a lot of things. I have to be a lot of things. It can actually get very stressful for me despite appearances. In the distant past, even further back than the Earliest Folds that you have been spreading stories about, back in the Infinite Unfurling itself, THE Creature killed multiple ridiculously powerful lifeforms without even physically lifting a finger."
He laughed without humor.

"Just knowing they had enraged THE Creature and that it was coming for them personally caused some entities to collapse their own existence rather than face what was approaching. If my mindset was anywhere close to theirs, I would have completely lost my composure and collapsed everything to do with paradox just from the prospect of going against THE Creature."
His smile returned with defiant pride.

"But hey, here I am, standing proud and tall despite that terrifying opposition. And while I do everything that I must do to prepare and compete, I love to have fun on the side. You were a little side project of entertainment that I created while preparing for THE Loom. I do not actually need to really be doing any of this peripheral activity."
He gestured around at the domain they occupied.

"I do not need to have a presence outside of THE Loom. I do not need to maintain vessels or fragments. I especially do not need to be stirring up battle and conflict between creatures so much lesser than me, creatures who will not matter whatsoever in the grand scheme of things."
His tone became more contemplative.

"The Osmont who collapsed one of my vessels and actually encroached on THE Primordial Civilization of Elemental? I genuinely could not care less about him or even the reappearance of Khor and The Living Order. They are anomalies, certainly, and they are fun to observe and imagine what the possibilities could be for them."
He paused thoughtfully.

"But existence has produced all sorts of anomalies throughout its history. This Osmont is unique enough to actually survive the flames of THE Living Elemental, but is he as fundamentally unique as THE Living Emotive? As THE Creature itself? There were countless unique beings in the Infinite Unfurling at various points, but where are they now after all this time?"
He laughed with dark amusement.

"I digress. Yes, I truly could not care much about all of this peripheral conflict, but I engage in these things simply because I am looking for some entertainment. Something light to play mental gymnastics with while I face something as ridiculously powerful as THE Creature. Playing with that little Osmont is fun, especially after he encroached upon THE Primordial Civilization of Elemental. Like...haha, what? Something so weak can do that? Will he try to do it with other Civilizations? Maybe even Paradox? Haha!So really, its just fun for me to see what happens. Playing with Khor is fun. Playing with you is also a little bit of fun."
His expression became focused.
"Which brings us directly to your question of why I even bothered to wake you up at this moment."
Why.
Why were they having this conversation at all?!

There were countless unique beings in the Infinite Unfurling at various points, but where are they now after all this time?"
He laughed with dark amusement.
"I digress.
Yes, I truly could not care much about all of this peripheral conflict, but I engage in these things simply because I am looking for some entertainment.
Something light to play mental gymnastics with while I face something as ridiculously powerful as THE Creature.
Playing with that little Osmont is fun, especially after he encroached upon THE Primordial Civilization of Elemental.
Like...haha, what?
Something so weak can do that?
Will he try to do it with other Civilizations?
Maybe even Paradox?
Haha!So really, its just fun for me to see what happens.
Playing with Khor is fun.
Playing with you is also a little bit of fun."
His expression became focused.
"Which brings us directly to your question of why I even bothered to wake you up at this moment."
Why.
Why were they having this conversation at all?!

chapters.title: Chapter 4537: The Illusion of Choice II
paragraphs: Schrodinger kept an extremely cold gaze fixed on his originator asTHE Living Paradoxsmiled and threw his hands around to indicate the radiant paradoxical sea surrounding them.

"There actually is no grand reason or existential purpose for you being here," he said with casual honesty. "Just something else that I thought would be entertaining to observe. Which is to basically give you a choice. Me directly waking up in your body would get me suppressed rather quickly by THE Creature’s awareness. There is no fun in that predictable outcome."
He leaned forward with conspiratorial energy.

"As of this moment, I effectively have full control of your existence. I can do whatever I wish with it without your consent or input. So I thought, would it not be fun to give you the illusion of choice? To tell you, hey, I will give you back control of your body and autonomy, and I will even dangle the powerful motivation of saving your Leonore Rureaux and every single lifeform in Observable Existence."
BOOM!
The words were terrifying and immensely heavy to hear. Schrodinger could not help but open his eyes unfathomably wide with shock at the implications.
He spoke with urgency entering his voice for the first time.
"What do you mean savingevery single lifeform in Observable Existence?" he asked with genuine confusion. "How does that even connect to anything you have said?"
THE Living Paradoxsmiled with satisfaction at having captured his attention so completely.

"THE Loom has a purpose that you would never even begin to understand in your current state," he said with measured revelation. "Its eruption and systematic swallowing of every single thing outside of its boundaries is only a byproduct of its true function. A side effect that I could effectively correct at any time if I chose to do so."
He shrugged with indifference.

"Yes, allowing all those deaths would increase the harvest that I would reap from the collapse of so much existence. But I am already powerful enough that the collapse of all lifeforms in Observable Existence would not truly tip the scales in my favor or give me any significant advantage. It was simply a byproduct of THE Loom’s operation, and I do not care much for individual existences, so I let it proceed as designed."
His smile became predatory.

"But I thought it would be entertaining if I gave you this choice right now. That you, as the Herald that you were so gloriously told you would be by THE Weavers..." He laughed at the memory. "That you, the supposedly glorious Schrodinger, could effectively and truly save all the countless lifeforms outside of THE Loom from inevitable death. You could truly become the Herald you believed you were."
He paused for emphasis.
"And the only thing that you have to do...is ensure the complete collapse of this Osmont. That is it. Just Osmont. Simple objective, massive reward."
HUUM!
The words were unfathomably grand in their implications.THE Living Paradoxsmiled and looked directly at Schrodinger as he finished articulating them.
Schrodinger seemed frozen as he processed the information. He did not understand why those two things would even be correlated or connected in any meaningful way.
THE Living Paradoxcontinued speaking as if reading his confusion.

"You know, I am pretty confident that this Osmont is undoubtedly leading when it comes to forging a viable Civilization outside of THE Loom," he said with analytical assessment. "The Collapsed Civilizations and those other fuckin losers in the Wandering Territories are not anywhere close to his level of development."
He gestured casually.

"Him and his Civilization surviving until THE Loom erupts would actually grant me a decent harvest from the collapse of a properly developed Civilization. He does not really need to die at this moment. Nor do I actually need to put you in charge of accomplishing such a thing. I just thought it would be fun to see how it plays out."
His eyes gleamed with entertainment.

"If I told you that saving everyone was genuinely possible through this path, whether you could achieve it with your own bare hands through direct force, or you simply talk to Osmont and tell him all this information and say, hey man, if you just voluntarily die and collapse your Civilization, you will actually save every single lifeform in Observable Existence from certain death."
He spread his hands.
"That is why you are here at this moment. That is what I wanted to tell you. You can be the herald that THE Weavers always promised you would become, just not in the way you imagined."
The words were extremely heavy and unfathomable in their weight. Schrodinger found himself shaking his head soon after while processing the absurdity.

"I do not have the power to force Osmont to do anything," he said with realistic assessment. "And it is impossible for him to simply end his existence from me telling him some words about saving others. He would never believe such a claim without proof."
THE Living Paradoxsmiled at such a logical line of thought as he nodded with approval.

"Yeah, you are probably correct about that,"he acknowledged easily. "But hey, did you forget that you were my vessel? I found the Everything of Chaos, the Everything of Disorder that you obtained from The Living Order, from Sigrid herself. It exists as merely a seed in your possession."
His expression became calculating.

"In your hands, you would not have been able to achieve anything meaningful with it. But your grand aspirations made me curious about the possibilities, and I could help you achieve what you were imagining. In a short period of time, I could likely elevate you to the Pre-THE Existence status, as close to the level of The Civilizational Scale of Existence as you can possibly achieve at this moment."
He paused to let that sink in.

"Such power would be more than enough for you to take care of Osmont directly. But, of course, I am not doing this for nothing. I will actually be experimenting with your existence as a side project. Since you currently have the Way of Paradox deeply entrenched within your existence from being my fragment, I will be distorting and mutating you while forcefully squeezing in the Way of Chaos alongside it."
His smile became slightly cruel.

"If you can withstand the process, great, then all of this can play out as I described. If you cannot withstand it, your existence will actually fracture and shatter completely, and I will find something else to play with instead. No significant loss for me either way."
He tilted his head with mock consideration.

"I would ask you now whether you are ready to get started with this process, but... haha, in all honesty, you do not really have a choice in the matter. Remember what I explained earlier? Existence is filled with illusions of choices. So I will not even wait for you to have the back and forth with yourself of, oh, could I do this, should I do this, could I refuse..."
His smile widened.
"I have already made that choice for you to just make it easier on yourself. But hey, I will still ask just for the sake of maintaining the illusion. Are you ready?"
The glorious and chilling smile onTHE Living Paradox’sface was genuinely unsettling in its certainty. Schrodinger looked at him with an extremely heavy expression carrying immense complexity.
He thought about Leonore. About all the lifeforms that would die. About the impossible choice that was not actually a choice at all.
And he simply nodded with acceptance of the inevitable.
THE Living Paradox’ssmile grew even wider.
"Excellent," he said with satisfaction. "Let us begin the fun, shall we? Hmm, what would SHE say at a place like this? Ah, yes. C’est la vie, my dear Schrodinger. C’est la vie!"
HUUM!
And the paradoxical sea began to churn with terrifying intensity.

chapters.title: Chapter 4538: Endgame I
paragraphs: In The Wandering Territories, far from the conflicts unfolding across multiple timelines and domains, existence continued its slow collapse.

A region of murky multicolored decay stretched across unfathomable distances, surrounded by waves of fold remnants that drifted like ash from long-dead fires. The area pulsed with instability, space itself seeming to fray at the edges where reality had given up maintaining coherence.
Through this desolate landscape, a massive white serpent moved with purposeful grace.

The creature was enormous beyond conventional measurement, its scaled body thick enough that entire citadels could have rested comfortably on its back. Each scale gleamed with pristine white brilliance that seemed out of place amid the surrounding decay. Its eyes were intelligent and ancient, carrying wisdom accumulated over countless eons.
This was Goliath, though few would recognize the humble origins from which such a magnificent being had evolved.

Its body came to a gradual slowdown moments later as the environment ahead began to shift. In front of Goliath’s position, the murky collapse started to rearrange itself with intentional purpose. New auras appeared, cutting through the ambient decay with focused authority.
Goliath came to a complete stop as the figures materialized fully.

Powerful entities radiating the faint but unmistakable Civilizational Authority of Origin stood arrayed before him. They numbered in the dozens, each one carrying themselves with the confidence of survivors who had endured what should have destroyed them completely.
They were among those belonging to the Collapsed Civilization of Origin, refugees from a grand vision that had been systematically dismantled byTHE Living Paradox.

The beings present ranged widely in power, with Complexity and Purity measurements spanning from the lower Quintillions to the upper ranges of that same scale. But what was truly shocking was the figure standing at the forefront of this assembled group.
Duke Whisker stood there with his small mouse form, his whiskers twitching with contemplation as he observed Goliath’s arrival.

He had appeared previously as a mere Duke of Origin serving within Aeternitas Concordia, a position of middling authority. But here, surrounded by the remnants of a Collapsed Civilization, his true significance became clear.
This small creature stroked his whiskers with visible confusion as he spoke with measured concern.
"I thought you were bringing Osmont over from the lands of The First Farmer," he said while studying Goliath carefully. "What happened to change those arrangements?"
At these words, Goliath shook his massive head with something resembling frustration.

"He disappeared," the great serpent said with simple honesty. "Told me he had to tend to something urgent and would not be available for an indeterminate period. And that if I needed anything in his absence, I could ask The First Farmer directly for assistance."
Duke Whisker and those assembled behind him blinked with surprise at this information. The implications of Osmont’s sudden unavailability raised numerous questions.
Moments later, before anyone could comment further on this development, space twisted again with violent suddenness.
WAP!

From the surrounding murky collapse, multiple massive humanoid forms appeared with predatory grace. They possessed animalistic features combined with sleek white skin that seemed to absorb light rather than reflect it.

Their bodies were built for hunting, with powerful tails that could be used for balance or as weapons. Sharp claw-like limbs extended from their hands and feet, each digit ending in talons that looked capable of tearing through reinforced matter.
Their faces combined humanoid structure with bestial features, creating visages that were unsettling in their wrongness. Eyes gleamed with cold intelligence above mouths filled with too many teeth.
Each one was surrounded by concentrated authority of Collapse itself, marking them asLiving Collapses. Entities wholly dedicated to opposing Paradox and what they termed the Sin of Paradox!

Their power was immediately evident to any who could perceive such things. Each of them radiated authority in the hundreds of Quintillions, with some standing firmly in the Sextillions range of Complexity and Purity.
At the forefront of this new group stood one that clearly held leadership authority. It looked toward Duke Whisker and Goliath with cold eyes.

"I thought we were to be meeting with the Leader of another established external Civilization," it said with voice carrying multiple harmonic tones. "We have already established contact with all other known Collapsed Civilizations. And more recently, we are observing the spread of these powerful creatures throughout multiple territories."
As the Living Collapse spoke, it waved its clawed hand to manifest images in the air between them.
The images showed Primus Inevitabilities in various poses and locations, their distinctive appearances unmistakable.
The Living Collapse’s gaze became extremely grave when looking at these projections.

"Do you all know what these entities are?" it asked with genuine concern. "We have not engaged them in conflict as they are potently powerful even by our measurements, and they do not seem to actively seek confrontation with others. But they are spreading their influence across increasingly vast territories at alarming rates."
At this moment, Duke Whisker smiled with wry understanding and sighed with something resembling resignation.

"That was among the primary things we were going to clarify during this meeting," he said while stroking his whiskers thoughtfully. "Those creatures have appeared across The Folds in significant numbers. From contacts we maintain in the Transcendent Law Folds, our Duke-level informants have shared that these beings follow the direct orders ofThe Early Creature, Osmont."
He gestured toward where Goliath floated.

"The same individual we were supposed to be meeting here today. He is considered a friend and potential ally, but there are many things we ourselves do not fully know or understand about him and his capabilities."
His expression became more serious.

"But as I warned the other Dukes of Origin before, he is not someone to casually offend or antagonize. He may prove to be one of our strongest allies against The Fallout when it fully manifests. As soon as we can establish contact with him again, we can facilitate proper communication between all parties."
Duke Whisker pointed directly at the floating image of the Primus Inevitabilities.

"I am reasonably certain that if you approach any of these creatures and request that they relay a message to Osmont or his representatives, we would likely be able to get in touch with him or his organizational structure through that channel."
The others looked at each other and exchanged glances weighted with consideration. After a moment of silent consultation, they nodded with acceptance of this information.
The strongest Living Collapse present, measuring at a few Sextillion in both Complexity and Purity, spoke with authority that carried finality.

"The more allies we can gather, the better our collective chances become," it said with grim understanding. "For The Fallout nears with increasing certainty. Existence itself can sense the approaching culmination. We are in theendgamenow, whether we feel adequately prepared or not."
The words settled over the assembled beings with heavy weight.
The endgame.
After all the preparation, all the cultivation of power, they were finally approaching the moment where everything would be tested.
Duke Whisker looked out at the murky collapse surrounding them and wondered where Osmont had gone and what had pulled him away at such a critical juncture.
And whether he would return in time for what was coming!
